Why You Should Still Buy Physical PS5 Games

I'll admit I'm a little biased here, but I really do think there's still plenty of life left in physical games. That's why Sony's plans to stop producing physical discs for new PlayStation releases from January 2028 are so disappointing. While existing physical releases won't suddenly disappear, the prospect of future PlayStation games becoming digital-only is a worrying one for anyone who enjoys building a collection.

Sony has attributed the decision to changing consumer preferences, so if we want physical games to stick around, we need to make our voices heard where it matters most: our wallets.

Buying physical gives you options that digital downloads simply don't. You can lend games to friends, trade them in, sell them when you're finished, or keep building a collection that you can actually see and hold. Physical retailers also compete with one another on pricing, meaning you're not entirely at the mercy of the PlayStation Store when hunting for a bargain.

There's a wider ecosystem worth supporting, too, from independent game shops and second-hand retailers to collectors and gaming preservationists. An increasingly digital-only future means fewer choices over where we buy our games, how much we pay, and what we can do with them afterwards.

So, if you've been sitting on the fence about picking up a physical copy of a game you've been eyeing, perhaps now's the time. Keep building that collection, support the retailers still selling physical games, and show Sony there's still an audience for discs. Buying a few games won't single-handedly reverse its decision, but if we stop buying them altogether, we're hardly going to convince anyone to keep making them.

Robert Anderson is a Senior Commerce Editor for IGN. Based in London, UK, he is a qualified journalist with a Bachelor of Arts in Journalism (First Class Degree) and over seven years of professional writing and editing experience.

You can usually find Robert lost in open-world RPG games like Elden Ring and Cyberpunk 2077. Outside of gaming, his passions include reading comics (especially Superman, Batman, and Spider-Man), taking photos, and keeping up with the latest in film and TV.

His primary coverage focuses on tracking down the best gaming deals and diving into the fast-paced world of Trading Card Games (TCGs). He regularly covers everything from the latest releases in Pokémon TCG and the most expensive cards to comprehensive Magic: The Gathering buying guides .

articles.title: 13-Year-Old Tekken Player Who Looks Just Like a Young Kazuya Mishima Defeats Fighting Game Pro in Stacked Tournament
articles.summary: A 13-year-old Tekken player went viral over the weekend for beating a seasoned pro in a competitive tournament — all while boasting a hairstyle that looked just like Kazuya Mishima’s.
articles.body:
A 13-year-old Tekken player went viral over the weekend for beating a seasoned pro in a competitive tournament — all while boasting a hairstyle that looked just like Kazuya Mishima’s.

Thaiger Uppercut (TGU) is a major fighting game tournament that takes place in Thailand each fall. It’s known for drawing some of the best talent across multiple titles from around the world, with established players flocking to the competition for fame, glory, and of course, prize money.

This year, however, an unexpected combatant emerged: 13-year-old Martinski, a Tekken player from the Philippines, left audiences stunned after taking out Pinya, a well-known Japanese Tekken pro who has been competing at a top level since the days of Tekken 7 .

HUGE round in pools. 📺 // #TEKKEN8 #TGU2026 — Bandai Namco Esports (@BNEesports) November 14, 2026

HUGE round in pools. 📺 // #TEKKEN8 #TGU2026

Martinski beat Pinya 2-0 in a stunning show of strength, knocking his opponent to the losers’ bracket. However, it wasn’t just the absurd talent he displayed at such a young age that made him go viral within the fighting game community; he also styled his hair to look like Kazuya Mishima, the Tekken series’ former protagonist-turned-antagonist.

In fact, Martinski made it to the Top 48 — a solid feat for a player of any caliber, but an especially impressive achievement for one so young. Looking at Start.gg, the 13-year-old competitor finished in 25th place out of 187 other players

Over on X/Twitter, Martinski spoke about his results, saying he was “proud of this run and grateful for the experience” and that “there's always something to take away from every tournament.”

@ELITE_Martinski IS INSANE AT TEKKEN 8 AND ONLY 13 YEARS OLD. CONGRATULATIONS FOR MAKING IT INTO TOP 48 AT TGU 🇹🇭 — Roo Kang (@rookang1) November 14, 2026

@ELITE_Martinski IS INSANE AT TEKKEN 8 AND ONLY 13 YEARS OLD. CONGRATULATIONS FOR MAKING IT INTO TOP 48 AT TGU 🇹🇭

Martinski also competed in a 3v3 teams bracket under the name ‘Martinski’s Magic Light Team.’ The group finished 9th out of 24 total teams.

Martinski’s performance at TGU highlights a growing trend within the fighting game community; young players are becoming increasingly successful in tournaments, particularly where Tekken 8 and Street Fighter 6 are concerned.

For example, 16-year-old Neia stunned audiences after making it to the Top 24 for Tekken 8 at Evo France, one of the most stacked tournaments of the season. She even beat established pros Hakim ‘Skywalker’ Touré and Jonathan ‘Tibetano’ Medina to get there, and has been a rising star in the scene ever since then.

And in Street Fighter 6, 17-year-old Chilean player Blaz recently helped his team win the Street Fighter League Americas Finals — but he’s been knocking heads since he was just 15, and even got second place at Capcom Cup 11 a few months after his 16th birthday. Another young Chilean talent, Craime, made the Top 8 at Evo Las Vegas this year at 15 years old, but has been competing in tournaments since he was 13. He famously won the Esports World Cup for Street Fighter 6 earlier this year, cementing his status as a major threat for the competition.

I got the chance to interview Blaz after his monumental victory with team 2Game after the SFL Americas Finals last weekend, where he explained why modern games like Street Fighter 6 attract younger players and why LATAM is such a strong region right now.

Virginia (she/her) is IGN’s News Editor. With ten years of experience reporting on games and entertainment, she’s got a storied background in the fighting game community, influencer news, and viral online trends. Find her on Twitter at @TheeMissGlaze .

articles.summary: In this Zelda: Ocarina of Time Remake boss fight guide, we show you how to defeat Twinrova, the final boss of the Spirit Temple. First, you'll need to face the sorceress sisters Koume and Kotake, who use fire and ice magic to attack Link. Their magical shields protect them from most attacks, so you'll need to use their own elemental spells against them. Reflect an attack with your Mirror Shield and redirect it toward the sister who uses the opposite element to deal damage.After hitting both sisters enough times, they'll combine into the more powerful Twinrova. Once her shield breaks and she falls onto one of the smaller platforms, rush in and attack with your Biggoron Sword. articles.title: 007 Fans React to Robert Pattinson's James Bond Casting
articles.summary: Robert Pattinson is the next James Bond, which means there is no shortage of opinions flying around the internet about this news.
articles.body:
Robert Pattinson is the next James Bond , which means there's no shortage of opinions flying around the internet about this news.

It was confirmed today that Robert Pattinson has been cast as James Bond , with reports saying his deal was squared away as recently as yesterday. Pattinson's casting was reportedly last-minute , as the producers have been working through an array of actors for Bond all year long. Pattinson only submitted himself for the part a few weeks ago when filming on The Batman Part 2 briefly paused . As a result, it shook up the group of finalists , which reportedly included names like Jack Lowden and Callum Turner.

With Pattinson stealing the gig with a buzzer-beater screen test and snagging a lucrative deal , it's no surprise that reactions have been animated, to say the least. The biggest takeaway for many is that Pattinson is playing both Bond and Batman, seemingly at the same time. Some joked that this is rather greedy of him, since he's an extremely accomplished actor and is hogging up some of the best parts.

The Next James Bonds Who Never Played 007

"Yo, I'm actually sick bro; that motherf**ker is gonna finish with a top 5 filmography ever," joked one fan .

"Being both Batman and James Bond, this is the greed they talk about in the Bible," said another .

Others think this may be a sign that his days as Batman are coming to an end. Of course, DC Studios bosses James Gunn and Peter Safran were just ousted from the company and replaced by a newer, cheaper alternative. It seems like Skydance may want to save on costs and also make more accessible movies, and it's unclear if the highly-expensive, dark, gritty Matt Reeves-directed Batman films will allow for that. It may be feasible to complete a trilogy if Reeves can get a third movie turned around quickly, but it took five years between the first two movies, and the sequel has experienced some setbacks, as well.

"He’s done as Batman after Part II, obviously," suggested an observer .

Although it's not impossible for an actor to do multiple movies in a year or in quick succession, Batman and Bond are extremely physical roles that demand a lot from an actor. Depending on schedules, it means Pattinson would have to constantly stay in tip-top shape, and he may not have time to do smaller films like he did with Primetime and The Drama this year.

The Batman Part 2 started shooting in late May or early June, and is expected to continue filming into early 2027. A Bond film has a similar extended schedule that also takes actors around the globe, limiting opportunities to do other projects. Maybe Pattinson will find a way to juggle both roles if DC wants a third installment, but the jury is out.

Although Pattinson's casting has been met with a lot of hype, others aren't as sold, given that he's become known for taking weirder roles. He's also been exposed to the audience a lot in the last year.

"Love Pattinson, but c'mon man, y'all have to cast unknown actors for some stuff," said a user on X . "I don’t see him fitting Bond.

"I just don’t see it," said another user . "Looks more like a villain than Bond"

Ultimately, though, Pattinson's casting as Bond is being met with a lot more enthusiasm than his initial casting announcement for Batman was. Although he'd turned in strong performances in films like Good Time before Batman, he was best known for being a sparkly, moody vampire in Twilight. For some, that didn't jive with their idea of Batman. Since then, he has been in a number of respected films that have reached wider audiences, including The Odyssey and soon-to-be Dune Part 3.

There's currently no release date for Pattinson's first Bond outing, though some expect it will release in 2028 with a 2027 shoot date in mind. Director Denis Villeneuve will likely be badgered with questions about the project when promoting Dune 3 in the next month, so we may get some more ideas of what to expect soon.

articles.title: Why Robert Pattinson Likely Can’t Play Batman and James Bond Together
articles.summary: Robert Pattinson taking on the James Bond role probably means that The Batman: Part II is his final outing as the Dark Knight. Here's why Pattinson likely can't (or won't) play both roles going forward.
articles.body:
Our long international nightmare is finally over. Amazon MGM Studios has selected a new actor to play James Bond, and it’s none other than former Twilight star Robert Pattinson . Despite being an actor who tends to prioritize quirky indie roles (while throwing in the occasional blockbuster for good measure), Pattinson has signed on to star in another of the film world’s biggest franchises.

This means Pattinson will now be in the unique position of playing both Batman and Bond. But can that arrangement last long-term, or is this a sign that the actor's days in Gotham City are coming to an end? Unfortunately, we think the latter possibility is the more likely one. Here’s why Pattinson is probably trading one superhero role for another, and why The Batman: Part II is almost certainly the end of the road for that particular series.

DC Universe: Every Upcoming Movie and TV Show

Pattinson’s Bond casting is certainly an interesting and unexpected development. MGM has tended to focus on up-and-coming actors for the various Bond films, whether it was a then little-known Sean Connery in 1962’s Dr. No or Daniel Craig in 2006’s Casino Royale. Early on, it seemed Amazon was going to continue operating under this philosophy , with relatively lesser-known actors like Callum Turner and Josh O’Connor emerging as frontrunners. Apparently, the studio had a change of heart.

Compared to past Bonds, Pattinson is already a huge name with a wide resume and multiple key franchises under his belt. This is basically like if the studio hired Christian Bale to take on the Bond role after 2005’s Batman Begins. It’s a lot of cinematic responsibility for one actor to shoulder.

Is there a world where Pattinson continues to juggle the dual responsibilities of playing Batman and Bond? Perhaps. The actor certainly seems to like keeping busy as an actor. In 2026 alone, he’s starred in The Drama, The Odyssey, and Primetime, and we still have his sci-fi heel turn in Dune: Part 3 coming up in December.

Still, it seems unlikely that even an actor as prolific as Pattinson is able or willing to juggle both James Bond and Bruce Wayne at the same time. Again, both roles are massive responsibilities that each require a huge time commitment, including the massive promotional push that comes after filming has wrapped.

Look at what happened to Mahershala Ali when he signed on to do Blade for Marvel Studios. Even though that project never came to be, Ali had to turn down a lot of work because he was so focused on training for the role and developing the film. Or look at Xochitl Gomez, who basically stopped getting offers after appearing in 2022’s Doctor Strange in the Multiverse of Madness because casting agents assumed she was too tied up in the Marvel machine.

Being James Bond and being Batman are both comparable. Each role can keep the actor tied up for months or years at a time. The odds that one franchise might interfere with the other in the years ahead seem rather high. With many years already having passed since 2021’s No Time to Die, Amazon MGM likely wants to push forward quickly with the reboot.

We highly doubt an actor like Pattinson, who clearly values his freedom to pursue interesting and unusual projects in this post-Twilight phase of his career, has any real desire to attempt to juggle both Batman and Bond simultaneously. This Bond news simply signals the idea that Pattinson feels his days as Batman are coming to an end. Currently, Steven Soderbergh has stepped in to finish production on The Batman: Part II while Matt Reeves deals with a personal matter. Once that wraps in late 2026 or early 2027, we’re guessing Pattinson will most likely hang up the cape and cowl and move on to other projects, one of which is the long-awaited James Bond reboot. He’s just trading one blockbuster franchise for another.

The Problem With Matt Reeves’ Batman Universe

Mind you, Pattinson may not be moving on from Batman out of a waning interest in the character, but simply due to the reality on the ground. There’s a lot currently working against this iteration of the Batman franchise. As mentioned, director Matt Reeves has had to step away from production due to personal problems. It’s unclear how heavy a role Reeves will have in the film’s post-production. We’re sure a third movie isn’t high on his list of priorities at the moment.

The likelihood is that if the newly merged Skydance even wants a The Batman: Part III, they’d have to push forward without Reeves as writer or director if they don’t want another long gap between sequels. Do fans actually want a Reeves-less The Batman: Part III? Would Pattinson even be interested in returning in that eventuality? Losing this series’ defining creative voice seems like too big a hurdle to cross.

And that’s assuming Skydance wants The Batman: Part III to happen at all. Right now, we have no idea what direction they’re taking with the DC line after firing James Gunn and Peter Safran. We’d argue the current DCU continuity should stay in place , but there’s no guarantee that’ll happen. All we can say for sure is that Batman, easily the most bankable DC character in existence, is going to be a major priority for the studio going forward.

It stands to reason that executives aren’t thrilled with how long it’s taken to put out a sequel to 2022’s The Batman. And they’re probably also not fond of the fact that Reeves’ The Batman movies exist in their own little universe, while the Batman of Gunn and Safran’s DCU is still an enigma after all these years. Historically, DC has always shied away from allowing multiple incarnations of characters to coexist in live-action, and that approach may continue under Skydance.

That leaves Skydance with two options - either focus on the Pattinson/Reeves universe as the sole Batman going forward, or reboot the character and pivot to something relatively more family-friendly and with more box office potential. We tend to think the company would opt for the latter. Incoming DC Studios head Jeremy Latcham seems to prefer more uplifting and family-friendly movies, and it would be in keeping with Paramount’s recent approach to the TMNT franchise .

Basically, between Reeves’ ongoing personal problems and the general direction of the wind at Skydance, there’s a good chance that there’s no future for the “ Batman Epic Crime Saga ” after The Batman: Part II finally arrives in 2028. We’re not holding our breath for The Penguin Season 2 either. That’s likely why Pattinson agreed to play James Bond. He sees the writing on the wall for his version of Batman, and he’s moving on to greener pastures.

It’s a shame in many ways, but we suspect that Skydance’s loss will be Amazon MGM’s gain in the years to come. Pattinson may not be the most bold or exciting choice to play Bond, but we can’t imagine he won’t do well in the role. There are far worse outcomes for this venerable franchise than to have Pattinson and director Denis Villeneuve rebooting it for a new era.

Jesse is a mild-mannered staff writer for IGN. Allow him to lend a machete to your intellectual thicket by following @jschedeen on BlueSky .

articles.title: Nvidia Reportedly Uninterested in Bringing Jensen Huang Back as CEO
articles.summary: Nvidia is reportedly not entertaining the idea of bringing Jensen Huang back as CEO following rumors that his allies had established a "war room" to push for his reinstatement.
articles.body:
Nvidia is reportedly not entertaining the idea of bringing Jensen Huang back as CEO following rumors that his allies had established a "war room" to push for his reinstatement.

The latest turn in the tech giant's whirlwind week arrived yesterday, when the Financial Times reported that the company's ex-boss had supported efforts from his friends in Silicon Valley to see him brought back into the fold . One source said these allies had assembled a "war room" to lay the foundation for his return, but it now seems those efforts may have been for naught.

The Nvidia board of directors is not considering reinstating Huang as CEO after he resigned from his position Thursday, November 12, one source told CNBC . Instead, company leadership is focused on the ongoing investigation launched after Huang confirmed he had an affair with a woman whom members of the U.S. government believed to be a Chinese spy on November 8.

The report states Nvidia hired law firm Wachtell Lipton to look into his relationship with the individual and how it may have compromised company secrets and/or national security. A message from the board added it had "no reason to believe that either national security or Nvidia secrets were compromised" when announcing the investigation last week.

One of the supposed goals of Huang's secret war room of Silicon Valley supporters was to gain White House support for the reinstatement – and it's a plan that seems to have panned out. U.S. President Donald Trump told reporters today (via Bloomberg ) that he "would not mind" seeing the embattled tech leader return.

"I would not mind. I would not mind that," he said. "I threw out the name of Tim Cook , but I would say that Jensen's reinstatement… I think he learned a big lesson. I guess maybe one lesson's more important than another, but I would certainly not mind seeing that."

Huang and Nvidia are now trying to pick up the pieces after the investigation began last week. The story so far has seen tech billionaire Elon Musk publicly back Huang , with some Nvidia employees saying they'd like him reinstated, too. Additional reports have said the former CEO had additional affairs with not one but two of his subordinates .

Earlier this year, Dell announced the "world's first 39" 5K monitor with RGB stripe tandem OLED technology." You can finally get your hands on one. The new Alienware AW3926QW has just been listed at Dell for $1,099.99 with free delivery. For Black Friday, Best Buy is offering it for $100 less . Save $100 Off the Alienware 39" 5K OLED Gaming Monitor

39" Alienware AW3926QW 5K RGB Stripe Tandem OLED Gaming Monitor

The Alienware AW3926QW has no lack of features that make it stand out from the crowd, but perhaps its most impressive technology is the RGB stripe tandem OLED panel. Tandem OLED stacks multiple OLED layers on top of each other instead of a single layer. Tandem OLED is better than other OLED panels because: 1) it's much brighter (the AW3926QW in particular has a very impressive 1,300 nits of peak brightness) and 2) it's less prone to burn-in.

The AW3926QW doubles down on this with new RGB stripe technology. Whereas traditional tandem OLEDs use white pixels, RGB stripe tandem OLED breaks the color down further into vertically aligned red, green, and blue pixels. This reduces color fringing and in turn significantly improves text clarity. It goes without saying that there are obvious benefits here for both gaming and productivity purposes alike.

Tandem and RGB stripe technologies aside, the AW3926QW is also Alienware's first 5K OLED monitor. With an impressive 5120 x 2160 resolution, this 39" monitor boasts a pixel density of 143ppi. That's even sharper than an already impressive 32" 4K monitor, with its pixel density of 138ppi. A 39" monitor is pretty wide, so the AW3926QW employs a 1500R curve to balance it out. 1500R is pretty moderate as far as curved monitors go, so although you'll be able to see the entire monitor within your field of view, it won't significantly distort peripheral images.

OLED monitors are known for their extreme fast response time and perfect black levels, making them ideal for gaming. The AW3926QW ups the ante with its 165Hz refresh rate at 4K and support for AMD FreeSync Premium Pro and NVIDIA G-Sync compatibility. It has both DisplayPort 2.1 and HDMI 2.1 ports so you'll be able to connect it to just about any modern day graphics card without the need for adapters.

Alienware also backs the monitor up with a 3 year warranty that covers OLED burn-in.

articles.title: Blizzard Tries 2 World of Warcraft Dungeon Fixes Over the Weekend to Stop Boosting Services
articles.summary: World of Warcraft Forever has now been out for a couple of weeks, and it's had a remarkably smooth launch. But now that players are starting to get to high enough levels to engage with dungeons, Blizzard is trying to nail down exactly how dungeons should reward players.
articles.body:
World of Warcraft Forever has now been out for a couple of weeks, and it's had a remarkably smooth launch. But now that players are starting to level up enough to engage with dungeons, Blizzard is trying to nail down exactly how dungeons should reward players.

Over the weekend, Blizzard pushed out a November 13 hotfix that made it so if there's any player in a group that's too high of a level to earn experience from monsters, no one in that group gets experience. The goal seems to be to get rid of boosting, where one high-level player can carry a group of players through dungeons to level them up quickly. But that solution backfired.

The problem is that in a lot of Forever's dungeons, there's a wide level range, so players on the high end of that range ended up accidentally nullifying everyone else's experience in the dungeon. That even happened to me on Saturday when trying to run Excavation Site with a level 37 player in my group.

The next day, Blizzard admitted that hotfix went too far. On the WoW Forever forums, community manager Kaivax posted , saying, "Yesterday, we updated dungeon play so that experience granted by an enemy in an instance is nullified if a high level player is in the group and enemy is trivial to that player. For some dungeons, the new restriction missed the mark because of the overall level range of the enemies in the dungeon."

Instead, Blizzard changed the way the restriction works. Rather than basing it on whether or not an enemy is "trivial" to any of the players, there's now a flat level difference restriction on experience. As Kaivax puts it, "We’ve just deployed a further change to this restriction, making it so that the XP nullification only kicks in when the high-level player is more than 12 levels above the level of the enemies."

For those who are just trying to do dungeons as they naturally come up while questing, the latest update should completely fix the issue, while also preventing boosters from powering people through the game. After all, Blizzard is dead-set on encouraging players to level out in the world, and is apparently not afraid of using some heavy-handed tactics to do so.

This also isn’t the first time that Blizzard has needed to adjust dungeon experience. Back when the WoW Forever beta first opened, the company severely limited the amount of XP you get from dungeons, only to buff it last week – even if it’s still far below what you’d earn in Classic . Blizzard has also changed the way gold is earned , in order to stop people from feeling like they had to hoard quest turn-ins for when they hit max level.

articles.title: Gerudo Proving Grounds Walkthrough - The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time Remake Guide - IGN
articles.summary: The Gerudo Proving Grounds (also known as the Gerudo Training Grounds) is an optional dungeon "mini-game" that Link can test his might at in The
articles.body:
The Gerudo Proving Grounds (also known as the Gerudo Training Grounds) is an optional dungeon "mini-game" that Link can test his might at in The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time Remake. Located near the Gerudo Fortress in the west of Hyrule, it can only be reached once Link is an adult, and after he has proven himself to the Gerudo people and earned the Gerudo Pass.

The Gerudo Proving Grounds is comprised of several challenging rooms featuring puzzles and dangerous enemies, many of which award Small Keys. These keys can be used to unlock a series of doors in a large central chamber, leading to the true reward of the Proving Grounds: The Ice Arrows.

While it's possible to obtain the rewards from this mini-dungeon with only a few key tools, completing every chamber and opening all optional locked doors will require Link to obtain the Silver Gauntlets at the Spirit Temple on the far side of Mirage Desert.

From the Gerudo Fortress, head along the large road to the southeast toward the horseback archery training course, and you'll find an attendant in front of a large gate who will tell you about the grounds. As an outsider, it will cost you 30 Rupees each time you want to enter the grounds and pick up where you left off.

As you enter, you'll find yourself in a large area with three large lion-shaped doors. The central door leads to the treasure room, which is filled with locked doors that progress in a maze-like fashion toward the center where the prize is.

If you inspect the room closely, you'll also find a hidden eye target above the entrance, which can be shot to reveal a Small Treasure Chest with a Blue Rupee!

The rest of the mini-dungeon is configured in a wide circle, with both doors leading to a series of rooms that connect at the top and loop around the central prize chamber, meaning you can head through in whichever order you wish.

Starting with the door to the right, you'll enter an arena lined by a wall of fire, pitting you against two Dinolfos and a Beamos sentry in the middle. If you can, quickly dash past the lizards to toss a bomb or set a Bombchu off at the Beamos before it can hamper you while you try and focus on the main adversaries. Note that if you've already completed the Spirit Temple at this point, you can also reflect the Beamos' laser with your Mirror Shield, and even redirect it at the Dinolfos!

If not, bait out their leaping sword attacks to render them vulnerable to counters, or use Deku Nuts to stun them and then follow up with a Spin Attack, as they have little defense to speak of. Defeating the pair will drop a small Treasure Chest down holding your first of many Small Keys.

Heading north, you'll enter the lava-filled room that will require the Goron Tunic unless you want to start burning alive! Five silver Rupees will appear in this obstacles course you'll need to traverse, with the first one just beside you.

With several Rupees floating in the air over the lava, having the Hover Boots in this room is recommended, though not entirely required, as you can also hookshot to several points along the walls. The second silver Rupees is between the middle and right ledge.

To the left is a high ledge with a door, and below it on one side is a switch, and on the far side, a third silver Rupee is engulfed in flames. Stepping on the switch turns the fire off for a short duration, but you'll still need a way over. Look for the nearby wall panel featuring a blue square, and play the Song of Time to create several large blocks. You can dash across to one using the Hover Boots and then climb up over the ledge to hover across to the Rupee before the fire returns.

Carefully hover back over to the ledge with the blue blocks and drop down to hover over to the north, and jump up the ledges to grab the fourth silver Rupee, and hookshot to the high ledge to pick up the final silver Rupee, opening the gate to the right.

Enter this room next, and you'll find a group of blue blocks in the center of the room. Playing the Song of Time will make them vanish, revealing a deep whirlpool below. For this, you'll need to ditch the Goron Tunic and Hover Boots, and instead adorn the Zora Tunic and Iron Boots instead.

First, focus on dropping to the very bottom, and using your Hookshot to defeat the two Shellblades in the corners of the room, so you can focus on grabbing all five silver Rupees down here.

One is located in the very center, and two others can be grabbed by using the hookshot targets along the walls. For the final two, you'll need to alternate your iron boots usage to swim up the corners and "fall" into them.

Grab all five, and a new gate will unlock revealing a small Treasure Chest with a second Small Key.

Return to the lava-filled room, where there are two other doors. The door above the blue blocks leads to the central prize chamber, and three small Treasure Chests holding three Arrows, five Bombchus, and a Small Key. However, we recommend that you DO NOT unlock the doors to the left, as they simply create a shortcut back to the entrance room, and effectively waste two keys!

This time, go to the far door on the north side of the lava-filled room on a high ledge. In the next room, you'll find several fiery enemies in a room filled with large stone statues. Use your bow to defeat the Fire Keese, and Megaton Hammer to squash the Fire Slugs. This will unlock a small Treasure Chest holding five Arrows.

To unlock the chest in the middle, use your Megaton Hammer to slam away all the segmented statues bordering the room. On the right side, you'll find one statue was on top of a small recess with a switch you can stand on to douse the flames, giving you access to your next Small Key.

Note that the far door leading out is barred, but you can unlock it by looking for an eye switch that was obscured by another statue along the wall. However, we'll be returning to to the entrance hall and taking the left path this time.

Entering the door on the left from the entrance, you'll be locked into an arena with several large stone pillars against two Stalfos. They'll wait to attack you one on one, and you can use this to your advantage by baiting out their jump attacks. Just be sure you have clear view of them and that they don't ambush you from behind the stone pillars. The sand can also make dodging difficult, so don't be afraid to lure them back to the stone platforms for better footing.

Defeat the pair, and you'll earn another Small Key.

Heading into the next room, you'll be in a large sloping area with a steady stream of boulders rolling down the sides, and five silver Rupees to claim. The path isn't as straightforward as you might think, as there are many hidden flame wall traps.

Grab the first silver Rupee in the back left corner after a boulder rolls by then quickly sprint back.

The second silver Rupee in the opposite corner has a flame wall in front of it, requiring you to move up the slope and then run down to claim it. From here, you can bypass the flame wall by using the hookshot target on the ceiling above the entry door, where the third silver Rupee is.

If you have the Longshot, you can reach the high ledge at the front from down below where the fourth silver Rupee is, otherwise you'll need to quickly run up the slope on the left.

Then, run up the remainder of the left slope to find the last silver Rupee in alcove blocked by another flame wall blocking the exit door, which you can bypass using the hookshot target on the ceiling.

This opens up the next room ahead, where you'll be locked into combat with two Wolfos and two White Wolfos. Try to remain mobile as you strafe around the outer part of the room to keep as many of them in view as possible. Backflip away from their swipes before jumping in on their exposed backs, and then reposition to re-target the next attacker.

Defeating the group will unlock a small Treasure Chest holding a Blue Rupee.

Now, you'll be met with two paths: One is a fake door you'll want to destroy, and then use the Lenses of Truth to reveal a hole in the wall above you can Hookshot to and find the true doorway out.

The second path is one that requires the Silver Gauntlets from the Spirit Temple to open, but if you don't have that yet you can skip it if you open the correct doors later, or just want to come back later. If you have the gauntlets, push the large black rock forward into a hole, revealing a sealed door. However, with the Lenses of Truth, you can spot an eye switch above it that you can shoot to open the door.

This leads to a gruesome room filled with Like Likes! Engage these foes cautiously, and use your long ranged tools to keep them from swarming you, or use the Hookshot to stun them before following up with a big spin attack.

You'll find that this room is full of a small Treasure Chests, but not all are worthwhile:

The one visible chest at the back of the room is actually an ice trap.

Defeating all the Like Likes causes a chest to appear by the front holding a Red Rupee.

You can bomb a cracked wall nearby to reveal another chest with five Bombs.

On the left side, there's an eye target on the high wall that will reveal a chest with a Business Scrub Seed.

The only real one you need can only be found with the Lenses of Truth, and holds the Small Key you're looking for.

Taking the door through the invisible gap in the wall above the fake door, leading to a large circular lava-filled room that you'll need the Goron Tunic to survive in.

Drop down below, and shoot the eye target above the door down here, which connect to the other path and that room with all the statues you needed to bash with the hammer. Hitting the eye target here will raise a large rock slab out of the lava covered in eye targets, while spinning the lower platform to create moving targets.

You'll need to hit all of the eye targets while moving along the platform, which will drain the lava, unseal the door above, and reveal a small Treasure Chest with a new Small Key.

To reach the high walkway again, look to the side of the door you just unsealed to spot a gust of straw, and play the Scarecrow's Song to summon Pierre. You can now hookshot up to enter the door, which leads back to the central prize chamber. This part however is an isloated area above it, and features one last small Treasure Chest with a Small Key to claim.

Now it's time to return back to the entrance and enter the central prize chamber. Before touching anything, check your total amount of keys:

If you only have 7 Keys, do NOT open the door on the right .

If you have 8 Keys, you can open the door on the right .

Accessing the door on the right will lead to a second locked door that serves as a shortcut to the lava-filled room you had to find silver Rupees in, as well as the few other small chests we opened previously. This chamber between doors also has a mesh wall you can climb up to a top floor, where you can spot a chest that can be accessed from the other side.

With this in mind, open the door on the left, and look for another mesh wall you can climb with an illusory ceiling leading to the second floor that hides the final key.

From this point on, as long as you have six keys left, you can open all the remaining doors leading to the center, each of which have their own small Treasure Chests containing a Purple Rupee, Red Rupee, and Three Arrows.

The last chamber in the very middle holds a large Treasure Chest, and within you'll find the main prize: The Ice Arrows.

With these, you'll be able to charge your magic power to unleash an icy blast at enemies and freeze many of them in place. This even has an added bonus effect on a few types of enemies:

Shoot at a Freezard to instantly melt and defeat it

Shoot at moving spike traps to freeze them in a harmless block of ice for an extended period

If you've gotten creative and haven't even completed earlier dungeons, you can even use it on Volvagia in the Fire Temple to stun and ground the foe by aiming at his head!

articles.title: How to Repair Guns - Rob Run Guide - IGN
articles.summary: Your guns and weaponry gradually break down as you use them in Rob Run. It's a way to ensure you're consistently spending money and have something to
articles.body:
Your guns and weaponry gradually break down as you use them in Rob Run . It's a way to ensure you're consistently spending money and have something to use as you continue to finance your criminal activities. As it stands, Rob Run is in early access, and gun repairs are not available in the current build. However, the development team has promised that they're on the way. Here's what we know about repairing guns and when it's coming to Rob Run.

The development team behind Rob Run did address this with its community. The team shared in a Steam news post released on Nov. 13 about the community's most frequently asked questions and addressed that gear durability degrading is a starting choice to help balance the in-game economy.

However, weapon and gear repair will be available in a future update. The team is planning to do it in a future weapon repair mechanic update.

A weapon's durability decreases every time you die. If you go down multiple times, expect the weapon to not function as well as it does when it's above the threshold. Whenever you defeat another player, you can inspect the durability by highlighting it while it's in your inventory. It will be under the weapon's magazine size and weapon range graph.

For now, though, any weapon that loses durability cannot be repaired in Rob Run. If there's a weapon you want to continue using, store it somewhere in your home, and wait for the weapon repair kits to become available. We'll also be updating this section when we learn more about how this gameplay mechanic works for everyone.

articles.title: Solo Beginner's Guide and Tips - Rob Run Guide - IGN
articles.summary: Running by yourself in Rob Run can be a challenge. Not only do you have to worry about fighting any players who are cops, but you have to avoid other player
articles.body:
Running by yourself in Rob Run can be a challenge. Not only do you have to worry about fighting any players who are cops, but you have to avoid other player criminals as well. They have an equal chance of ambushing you and taking your stuff when you're attempting to rob or get a fence to buy your items. In this guide, we're going to go over essential tips and tricks that you should know about playing solo in Rob Run.

When you're playing as a Solo player, you automatically receive a passive effect in Looty Bay. Whenever you enter as a Criminal, you begin at Notoriety level 4, where you have increased chances for additional loot, items, and money for you to acquire.

The added risk is that you're by yourself, and likely in a lobby with players who are roaming around together. You'll need to play it safe and carefully if you want to get out with your hard-earned loot. Her

Purchasing and unlocking larger bags for you to carry is a great way to make sure you can always grab as much as you can from every robbery site. A small upgrade to your kit that would be a large stepping stone is the Sports Bag

It's one of the first Equipment upgrades you can get from the Shipments tree. After unlocking it, the Sports Bag only costs $5,000. That's not a huge amount after you've been running for a bit and completing a handful of smaller robberies. It should make fitting every item you find at a location in your inventory, as it adds 12 slots. You might get a few runs in before you lose it to other players or cops, but that can more than make up for it and allow you to purchase more.

If you acquire a large pile of money, putting it towards upgrades is the best investment you can make in Rob Run. These give you access to better items, gear, and weapons that should make it easier to survive taking on multiple players at the same time.

The first Settlement is the biggest hurdle, but saving up for the second one is even more daunting. After your first Settlement house purchase, consider working on unlocking a new car, like the Fukurou Tensa. The increased speed and acceleration should make it easier to outrun players and cops, increasing your chances of escaping a high-speed chase.

What can help you most is knowing when to escape Looty Bay. Knowing locations that you can rob and then make a quick escape is always good to prioritize. You also want to improvise and change your plan based on the server you enter. Riding around the map to notice what locations players are already robbing or where cops are heavily patrolling is a good idea.

You only have two exits in Looty Bay, from the southwest and the southeast bridges out of town. For most runs, it might be better for you to focus on gathering up as much loot as you can carry in your inventory and car before leaving, and not going to a fence immediately. Directly going to a fence increases the chances of someone catching you halfway through, and you lose everything. By returning to Looty Bay after you rob a place, you can choose a fence and immediately become a Criminal, rather than doing it in one swoop.

Every time you bring any money or items you've collected from Looty Bay, they go directly into your house. Although you are the only person who can go onto your property, there's a chance for other players to use Decoders to break your defenses. A Decoder is a rare item, but if another player wants your items (and they have enough Decoders), they can break in.

The best defense that you can use in these scenarios is to add fuses to your fence and your primary building. Fuses are how you improve the home defense bonuses you get and increase the number of Decoders that other players have to use. Unlike Decoders, fuses are available on the Black Market, making them easier to acquire and a worthwhile upgrade to everything you own.

You'll find multiple small robbing locations throughout each part of Looty Bay. These include tech shops, convenience stores, jewelry departments, and small houses. Although these locations are small, they are effective and quick to clean out.

If you want to prioritize how much loot you get from each one, having a key or a way to unlock the safes here provides the best loot. A safe in any of the department stores gives you a good chance of finding Epic or Legendary loot that you can sell for a high price at any of the fences.

Although being a Criminal gives you the most money in Looty Bay, playing as a cop is a good way to take a break and track down other players. What's really nice is that when you get eliminated by another player, you don't lose any items. Instead, you go back to the police station and try again.

Cops play an important role in stopping criminals from stealing in Looty Bay. When you catch a criminal, they'll drop a bag and all of their loot on the ground when you haul them off to jail. Alternatively, the players can try to bribe you, which is another way for you to earn money if you want to gain an income that way. Playing as the Cop is a good way to try the less stressful part of Rob Run and earn a steady income with far less risk.

Like the escape routes in Looty Bay, the fence dropoff sites where you sell your contraband remain at specific spots in the city. They don't move around, and don't randomly appear. Instead, everyone knows where to find them, making it easy for other players to camp these locations and potentially ambush you.

It's a common sight to witness, unfortunately. The only thing you can do is patrol these locations as a civilian, and wait to see if the coast is clear. You might even want to roam around to double-check that the dumpsters are not full. What's nice is that you don't lose anything if you're a civilian. If someone takes you out while you're a civilian, before you become a Criminal to sell your items, you keep everything.

articles.title: Christopher Nolan's The Odyssey Comes to Digital With Over 90 Minutes of Bonus Features
articles.body:
Christopher Nolan’s The Odyssey has landed on digital platforms .

The move to digital comes exactly four months after the movie’s initial release in theaters, making it the longest theatrical window of 2026. Why would you rush the digital release for a movie that keeps selling out ?

If you somehow didn’t catch the movie in theaters, or are already itching for the at-home rewatch, here’s where to find the movie on digital as well as all of the info we have about The Odyssey’s streaming and home entertainment releases.

The Odyssey is now available to rent or purchase digitally ( see at Prime Video ). Choosing to purchase the movie will net you over 90 minutes of bonus features across 12 behind-the-scenes featurettes.

The Odyssey, which boasts a full runtime of almost three hours , is legendary director Christopher Nolan’s take on Ulysses’ epic. Matt Damon stars as Odysseus, while future Bond himself , Robert Pattinson, goes full weasel mode in the role of Antinous.

This is Nolan we’re talking about, so the movie can be aptly described as a full spectacle. The man is very dedicated to his special effects, which are in full display across The Odyssey’s mythology-inspired sequences.

IGN’s review goes so far as to call it a "must-watch cinematic experience," and audiences appear to have felt the same way. After multiple extensions , The Odyssey has grossed over $1.5 billion, making it second only to Spider-Man: Brand New Day as the highest-grossing movie of the year.

The Odyssey was the first movie shot entirely in IMAX cameras, and was shown in a number of different formats while in theaters. The digital release will have a 1.78:1 (16:9) aspect ratio to approximate the original IMAX format that isn’t natively supported on digital media platforms.

If you weren’t able to make it to the theaters, or just want to relive that specific experience, keep an eye out for more IMAX showings coming this December . Otherwise, your best bet is picking up the 4K disc edition. The 4K steelbook is currently sold out, but standard 4K, Blu-ray, and DVD releases are still available. These are also out on November 17, the first 'full day' the movie will be available on digital.

As a Universal release , The Odyssey will eventually stream on Peacock. Recent Universal releases have come to streaming around three months after their initial release date, which would have put The Odyssey’s streaming release date about a month ago. Like the delayed digital release, Universal is likely holding off on the streaming release to promote the digital and home video releases for a couple more months.

articles.title: GTA 6 Global Release Times Confirmed: Here's How to Play Early Via the New Zealand Trick
articles.summary: GTA 6 will have a regional release, which means certain people can actually play it early thanks to what's called the New Zealand trick. Here's how it works.
articles.body:
GTA 6 will have a regional release, which means certain people can actually play it early thanks to what's called the New Zealand trick.

Rockstar Games has confirmed that GTA 6 will become available at midnight local time, as the clock strikes November 19, meaning some parts of the world will get the game earlier than others. Xbox has a pretty well-known loophole known as the New Zealand trick, which allows you to play games a full day early with ease.

How to Do the New Zealand Trick for GTA 6

All you have to do is open your Xbox's settings menu, scroll down to System, and click on Language and location. Change the location tab to New Zealand and hit the "Restart Now" button on the right-hand side of this menu to reset your console. When you come back online, your console will be "in" New Zealand. As a result of this, make sure to buy GTA 6 before you change your console's location; otherwise, you will have to pay in New Zealand currency.

As for PlayStation, there is also a New Zealand trick, but it's not nearly as easy or convenient. You have to create a new account based in New Zealand and buy a copy for that account. You can then enable game sharing to give the game back to your main account, but you will likely need to play the game on the New Zealand profile until it unlocks for your regular account. So, it may be too much of a headache to even bother with this on PS5.

For those in the United States, using the New Zealand trick lets you play GTA 6 almost a full day early, at around 7am ET on November 18. This trick applies to those outside of the United States as well, but folks in the U.S. will arguably get the most mileage out of this, and playing early will help with the inevitable spoiler problem as GTA 6 goes live around the world ahead of you.

If you're avoiding the New Zealand trick, you'll need to wait until midnight local time.

GTA 6 global release times on PS5 and Xbox Series X and S:

Denver (Mountain): 10pm MST (November 18)

Chicago (Central): 11pm CST (November 18)

As is well documented, GTA 6 is not being released on-disc. Rockstar Games has released a 'code-in-box' version that is available now. So, all will have to download GTA 6, which weighs in at 212GB. Rockstar will sell a double-sided map/poster for 99 cents on its online store. It will also be included for free with purchases from the company's store, but fans can also download and print out a free one as well if they want.

While you wait for GTA 6 to unlock we've got loads of great coverage for you to check out, including Gangland Tales From the Frontline of Rockstar's Real-Life Grand Theft Auto Research , and How Gaming's Top Content Creators Are Preparing for GTA 6's Launch and Beyond .

articles.title: Sony Squeezes in Last-Minute PS5 Firmware Security Update Ahead of GTA 6 Release Date, Amid Fresh Hacker Claim
articles.summary: Sony has released a new PS5 firmware security update just a day before the release of GTA 6, and hot on the heels of a new claim from a prominent hacker around the console.
articles.body:
Sony has released a new PS5 firmware security update just a day before the release of GTA 6 , and hot on the heels of a new claim from a prominent hacker around the console.

PS5 system software update 26.07-14.23.00 is available now, weighing in at 1.267 GB, and according to Sony’s official patch notes , it makes “some security fixes to the system software.”

Today’s update comes just two weeks after PS5 firmware update 26.07-14.22.00 came out , which itself was released just 11 days after the release of 14.20.

The PlayStation homebrew scene has made headlines in the last two months for releasing PS5 jailbreaks for prior firmwares. For example, late September, a jailbreak that supported all PS5 consoles running firmware 7.00-13.60 sent shockwaves through the homebrew community because, at the time, it meant that all PS5s, including the PS5 Pro, that hadn't been updated within the previous week were compatible with the jailbreak. This was of huge significance for Sony and the security of the PS5, as people with a jailbroken PS5 can modify their console, potentially opening the door to video game piracy.

However, it was found that some PS5 games subsequently required the more recent 14.00 firmware in order to download updates, sparking a renewed effort to release a new jailbreak for the updated system software. So, there is a game of Whac-A-Mole at play where the homebrew scene is working to release a new jailbreak for the latest PS5 firmware, then do it all over again when Sony releases a new firmware update designed to beef up security.

This in turn has sparked concern that if a PS5 jailbreak was made available for the firmware that is required by GTA 6, then it may be possible for Rockstar’s game to be pirated on PS5 and maybe even made available on PC.

14.23 released today just a day after a prominent PS5 hacker claimed to be the first person to have “dumped” a game binary at 14.22. While this wasn’t necessarily evidence of a full jailbreak for PS5 on that firmware, it did send the homebrew community into speculation overdrive on whether Sony would react quickly.

There’s no evidence to suggest this latest firmware update was in response to the latest development, and it is not yet confirmed whether 14.23 will be required to play GTA 6. But it’s hard not to view it as yet another attempt to close the circle ahead of GTA 6’s release.

GTA 6 preload launched last week, but Rockstar Games has continued to update it in recent days. The question for Sony is whether it can do enough to eventually win this game of Whac-A-Mole with the homebrew scene. This is something of an existential crisis for Sony, which publishers and developers rely upon for the security of their PlayStation releases. But with the emergence of powerful AI models, the stakes have risen significantly.

Just last week, Strauss Zelnick, the CEO of Rockstar parent company Take-Two, told IGN that the company was taking security seriously , and insisted that fans will prefer to play GTA 6 officially, with all its bells and whistles as Rockstar intended, over an unofficial PC version.

During an investor-focused Q&A, Zelnick was asked multiple times about this AI reverse-engineering problem. He, again, had strong words in response, suggesting Take-Two was ready to lawyer up.

“This business has been largely immune to piracy concerns forever because of file sizes, complexity of piracy, being connected to servers and the like,” he began. “And undoubtedly, it would be very difficult to replicate the experience of consuming our game as intended because of technical limitations.

“That said, it's going to become more of a challenge, as you said, and we're aware of that. So we are utterly focused on enhancing our technical defenses and enhancing our legal activities appropriately. And at the same time, without in any way being cavalier, every entertainment business that exists is subject to some element of piracy. So this is likely to invade our business to a greater or lesser extent. I think it will be manageable and we are focused on it.”

IGN reported on a hacker who had sparked an uproar within the PS5 homebrew scene for privately reporting an exploit to Sony and cashing in on a $50,000 reward, rather than keeping it confidential for the community.

articles.title: Marvel Boss Kevin Feige Addresses Jonathan Majors' Firing, Insists It Was Always the Plan to Eventually Replace Kang With Doctor Doom
articles.summary: Kang was always set to be replaced by Doctor Doom as the main villain of the Multiverse Saga, Marvel boss Kevin Feige has insisted — regardless of Jonathan Majors' high-profile firing.
articles.body:
Kang was already set to be replaced by Doctor Doom as the main villain of the Multiverse Saga, Marvel boss Kevin Feige has insisted — regardless of Jonathan Majors' high-profile firing.

Before Majors' swift ditching by Disney in the wake of assault and harassment charges, the Multiverse Saga's first Avengers movie was due to be titled The Kang Dynasty, with Majors' Kang the Conqueror taking on Earth's mightiest heroes in a Thanos-style role. The film was instead subsequently retooled and retitled as Avengers: Doomsday , with Robert Downey Jr. then announced as returning.

But rather than this pivot being completely unplanned, Feige has now claimed the change had already been on the cards — even if the way it was presented was disrupted after Majors' exit. Indeed, Feige argued that Doom's introduction was already being hurried along after the failure of Ant-Man and the Wasp: Quantumania, which underperformed at the box office despite featuring Kang front and center.

A Time-Bending Look at Kang the Conqueror's History

"Quantumania was not received the way we would have liked," Feige told Empire magazine. "There are many elements of that that we're proud of, the Kang performance being one of them. But we were changing [The Kang Dynasty] even at that point. It would still have been called The Kang Dynasty, but it would have been a set-up for Doom, midway through that movie."

The interview marks the first time Feige has properly addressed Majors' departure in detail. Disney parted ways with the rising star immediately after he was found guilty of assaulting his then-girlfriend, though there had been a growing expectation in the lead-up to Majors' sentencing that the problematic actor was set to be jettisoned. Still, questions remained over how Marvel would handle the Kang storyline, which had been heavily seeded in Loki and elsewhere by that point.

"It was very delicate," Feige continued. "We didn't want to rush into any rash decisions in terms of employment. People think there was a cause-and-effect with Jonathan's issues, and that certainly accelerated some things. But the Doom of it all was well underway before that."

Will Doomsday address Kang at all? This remains to be seen, though Marvel's policy up until now appears to be ignoring that the Kang storyline ever took place, in favor of Doctor Doom instead.

Avengers: Doomsday is set to premiere December 18, 2026, meaning we're only weeks away from its release date. Last week, we learned that Deadpool and Wolverine stars Hugh Jackman and Ryan Reynolds have writing credits on the movie . Feige also debunked one of the biggest theories regarding potential connections between Downey's Tony Stark and Doctor Doom .

The 2.6.0 Patch for ARC Raiders has arrived, bringing with it dozens of general improvements and fixes to update game performance, balance and general stability.

This page acts as a comprehensive breakdown of the 2.6.0 Patch for ARC Raiders, including a link to the full Patch Notes.

Fixed an issue where being latched by a Tick while depositing a Fuel Cell could break animations and prevent interactions such as breaching or using weapons.

Improved proximity chat reliability on Steam Deck.

Softened the Gondola Transceiver alarm for Ballistic Gondola calls to be less jarring.

Fixed an issue where the Scorta Helmet toggle 'On' failed to unlock after obtaining Wildcard II rank.

Fixed an issue where the player could appear invisible if they entered then quickly exited the Gondola.

Fixed an issue where the Road Warrior skill could not recycle Weapon Amplification Modules or Candleberries during raids.

Fixed an issue where vaulting also drained jump-stamina, and the “Vaults on Vaults on Vaults” skill no longer drains any stamina.

Fixed an issue that could cause players to appear invisible during a round.

Fixed an issue where starting a knockout on a downed Raider could move you and push you through walls. You now remain in place during the knockout animation.

Fixed a bug where enemies could knockout a player immediately after they were revived with a defibrillator; being revived now properly prevents knockouts.

The Hydra will now only aim some of its weapons against Lure Grenades. It will still target players while also firing some guns at the lure.

When activating many Firework Boxes at the same time, instead of some boxes fizzling out, they now delay shooting their rockets. This means that, if you’re trying to create firework shows, their duration can be extended by activating more Firework Boxes.

Updated Snap Hook description to reflect the correct range of 18m (previously stated as 20m).

Fixed an issue where a thrown Grapple Hook line could persist after being downed; the hook now cancels correctly mid flight if you are blocked from firing or when you go down.

Fixed an issue that caused players to be thrown into the air when the Grapple Hook cable collided with another object before reaching its destination.

Fixed various collision issues around Pendola Pass, Spaceport and Riven Tides.

Fixed an issue where the Access Capacitor rack and dropped batteries could sometimes lack an interaction prompt, preventing pickup—these can now be interacted with correctly.

Reintroduced Cold Snap to the Major Map Condition rotation!

Fixed an issue where you could not shoot through the windows in the railyard.

Closed a gap in the world where players could fall in behind a cliff and get stuck inside on Pendola Pass.

Additional fixes to surfaces and collisions inside the Emperor.

Refined lighting and atmosphere on Spaceport to improve visibility when looking from interiors to exteriors, reduce harsh contrast, enrich overall color tone, and speed up exposure adaptation for clearer readability.

Improved lighting and exposure on Buried City to enhance visibility in dark interiors and when looking from indoors to outdoors; reduced extreme contrast and cloud shadowing, with a more natural color tone and subtle bloom adjustments.

Additional improvements to collision around the Seed Vault Airshaft in order to prevent players from glitching their way inside.

Fixed an issue that could cause certain quests to soft lock if the required quest item was lost.

Resolved an issue where a short press could leave the Ping Wheel stuck open, preventing player input.

You can now drop items by dragging them outside of your inventory, no longer requiring you to drag them to a designated area.

Fixed an issue where LB/RB bumpers wouldn’t change tabs in the Inventory while at the Outpost; button prompts now match and bumper navigation works as expected.

Fixed an issue where the Repair button could become unresponsive when opened from the Inspect screen for damaged weapons.

Fixed an issue where returning to the Level tab on the End of Round screen could show your previous level instead of the level you just earned.

Fixed an issue where Mouse 4 and Mouse 5 thumb button icons appeared reversed after reassigning keybinds.

If a weapon that is given as a reward comes with a stencil applied, the icon now correctly displays that stencil.

Fixed an issue where looting with a gamepad could cause the selected item to disappear if you were interrupted (e.g., by a Tick). Also resolved a case where splitting an item into the same slot could delete the stack.

Fixed an issue where some furniture slots in the Outpost could not be selected from certain camera angles or when overlapping with other stations; selection boxes now better match the items.

Fixed an issue where the “skill point available” indicator could remain visible after spending all Skill Points.

Adjusted several furniture slots in the Outpost to prevent objects clipping into walls and to reduce camera issues when accessing Scrappy nearby.

Added the option to track resources for Project steps from any page, including when previewing steps.

Fixed a niche situation where the Outpost could not be completely upgraded. The Outpost can now be correctly upgraded to Level 4.

The Reward Pass screen now cycles between multiple background images to preview pass content.

Added the Show/Hide Tooltip prompt when browsing bundles with multiple color variants in the Store using a gamepad.

Fixed an issue where the stars-earned pop-up in Trials would not appear when scoring above your personal best; it now displays correctly.

Added a “Times Revived By A Stranger” stat to the Codex player stats page.

Reduced the weight of the Stiletto from 7 to 6.

Fixed an issue where the crosshair sometimes failed to indicate that a shot is not being blocked anymore while moving sideways aiming at an ARC.

Fixed an issue where aiming down sights with scoped weapons could shift aim sideways; aim now stays aligned with the crosshair when entering and exiting ADS.

articles.title: The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time Remake Is Already Running Rampant on PC — but Can Nintendo Do Anything About It?
articles.summary: The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time remake is running rampant on PC, but can Nintendo actually do anything about it? We asked legal experts to find out.
articles.body:
Shortly after the release of The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time remake , players quickly found ways to start playing it on PC.

This was done through a few different methods. One is through an emulator, whereas others are through recompilation tools, which run the game natively on PC without emulating the Switch 2. Either way, the people who make these emulators and tools insist that users have to supply their own game files, so the downloads won’t work on their own. In other words, they want you to buy the game before you start playing it on PC, to cover their backs.

This is nothing new for a big release, but we’ve never seen it done so quickly before. That’s because many of these emulators and tools were AI-assisted, which is also why you have seen so many other “native” PC ports of games floating around (to mixed results — and fears concerning how safe they actually are to play).

But it’s these PC ports of Ocarina of Time that have gotten the most attention. Some players have even managed to get an unofficial multiplayer release going, mere days after the game launched on PC.

The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time Remake Launch Photos

There's a lot to say about these, but debates over quality or AI usage aside, the most obvious question is: will Nintendo put up with this? The company is notoriously litigious and has successfully sued emulators before. It even started taking down Nintendo Switch 2 emulators earlier this month, so many would assume that it is only a matter of time until it does something about the Ocarina of Time craze.

However, according to legal experts speaking with IGN, it won’t be a clear-cut case for Nintendo.

“The basic arrangement of the emulator as just being a piece of software capable of running games that you have to provide separately is critical,” Kirk Sigmon, founding partner at KellDann Law, told IGN. “At least in theory, the law is very favorable towards emulators.”

He went on to cite a case from 2000 in which Sony unsuccessfully sued the creator of an original PlayStation emulator. “[This case] basically indicates that emulators are (on their own) legal and the reverse engineering of game consoles can also be legal, even when performed in a manner that might otherwise arguably infringe copyright law,” he argued.

This could apply to all the tools being used to play the Ocarina of Time remake on PC, including the popular new emulator, Lichii. “If it was developed using AI and without stealing trade secrets, and if it’s carefully managed to never include Nintendo’s other IP, it’ll be hard to stop,” Sigmon said.

Others, such as Zohaib Hashim, CEO of Blackmont Legal, echoed this sentiments. “I do not believe that [emulator/decompilation creators] can be said to be breaching copyright or infringing on Nintendo's IP simply by virtue of developing and supplying emulator software,” Hashim said in an interview.

“Emulators generally are legal; there's established case law going back many years supporting this,” he continued, citing the same Sony lawsuit.

With that said, Sigmon admitted that Nintendo won’t take this lying down. “Nintendo is absolutely going to try to shut Lichii and/or the decompilation teams down,” he predicted. “Nintendo is likely looking for any possible justification for going after them: the accidental use of some art/music asset, the inadvertent use of a logo, evidence that they stole some sort of trade secret, or the like.

“There’s even a possibility that they’ll try to shut them down for orthogonally related activities, like uploading videos of emulated game content on YouTube. After all, some gamers are already enjoying the Ocarina of Time remake on their computers mere days after the game was released. That can’t be good for the game’s sales targets.” Just days after we spoke, Nintendo started to get videos showing the Ocarina of Time remake PC port removed from YouTube over copyright claims.

Other experts I spoke to highlighted possible flaws in the creators’ defence. Michael Dilworth, managing partner of Dilworth IP LLC, said that insisting users supply their own game “only gets them so far.”

“Emulation itself is not inherently unlawful under U.S. copyright law,” Dilworth said. “The more difficult issue involves the Digital Millennium Copyright Act (DMCA), which restricts the circumvention of technological protections and the distribution of certain circumvention technologies.”

In other words, Nintendo could dive into how these tools work, rather than solely complain about the fact that the emulator exists at all. “Nintendo relied heavily on that statute in its case against Yuzu, and its recent enforcement activity suggests that circumvention remains central to its legal strategy,” Dilworth said.

What About The People Using The Emulator?

On the whole, it seems to be agreed that those operating emulators or recompilation tools have a decent defence, so what about the people using them?

That’s where we see a difference in opinion. I raised the point with Sigmon that Switch 2 users have to sign an end-user licence agreement (EULA), which could be breached by decompiling legitimately purchased projects. He did not feel that Nintendo had a leg to stand on here.

“That’s just words on a page that Nintendo would have to try to actually enforce in a court or some sort of arbitration tribunal,” Sigmon said. “Such enforcement would introduce a lot of hurdles — for example, it’s possible that someone might buy a Nintendo Switch 2 and use it for reverse engineering purposes without ever agreeing to Nintendo’s EULA.”

However, Hashim came at this issue from another angle. “Circumvention of DRM protections are considered an infringement, and there isn't a permitted purpose for decompiling the code for this specific purpose,” he argued. “The decompiling of the code may additionally be a violation of Nintendo's EULA and TOS, which entitles them to cancel the licence granted to the infringing party.” He also stressed that this applies regardless of whether you bought the game physically or digitally; either way, you bought a licence for the game.

Marcus Denning, principal and senior lawyer at MK Law, also made this case. “Owning a legitimate copy of a Nintendo game does not necessarily give a user permission to bypass the console's technical protections,” he said, adding that this applies whether or not you go on to share the files with others. “Copyright law addresses activities such as reproducing and distributing protected works. Separate provisions may also apply when technological measures used to control access to copyrighted material are bypassed.

“Ultimately, purchasing a legitimate copy of a game is only one part of the legal question. How the emulator operates and how users access the game files also matter under the applicable copyright laws.”

What is more complicated is the legality behind sharing advice on how to play Ocarina of Time remake on PC.Sigmon said that, according to the law, content creators could in theory be free to upload videos showing exactly how they got their legally purchased copies of the game playable on PC.

However, Dilworth expressed some concern: “Explaining how software works or examining its underlying functionality isn't necessarily unlawful. But distributing tools or instructions specifically designed to defeat technological protections can raise additional legal concerns under the DMCA.”

Does It Matter That Nintendo Has Done This Before?

With all of this said, we all know that Nintendo has successfully taken some emulators down. For instance, Yuzu was shut down after being sued by Nintendo, resulting in a $2.4 million payout in Nintendo’s favor .

If Nintendo wants to take on emulators and decompilers using the same method, I’m told that it would have to prove that they are actively bypassing protections put in place by Nintendo.

“The case was Nintendo of America v. Tropic Haze LLC, and it essentially focused on Yuzu’s action of decrypting game files immediately before and during runtime using copies of Nintendo Switch-derived cryptographic keys,” Sigmon explained. He said it is “unclear” if Nintendo could use the same argument with the tools being used to play Ocarina of Time on PC.

“LLM [AI] tools have made it far, far easier to develop emulators without necessarily needing to circumvent anything and/or pilfer any trade secrets, and my understanding is that the current ROMs floating around of Switch 2 games are already decrypted,” he continued. “If that’s true, and if Lichii is just playing those already-decrypted ROMs without circumvention, they might be in a better position than those in Tropic Haze [creator of Yuzu].”

Dilworth, meanwhile, noted that some of these projects, including Lichii, are built on Yuzu’s work, which could be brought up in court. “That connection matters because Nintendo successfully pursued Yuzu's developer in 2024,” Dilworth said. “But the case was resolved without a trial, so it didn't establish that video game emulators are generally unlawful.

“Simply using code derived from Yuzu doesn't automatically make Lichii unlawful. But if Lichii retains functionality that Nintendo previously challenged, I would expect Nintendo to raise similar legal arguments.”

He also believes that Nintendo is likely to take action, saying that Lichii has “good reason to be concerned.”

Whatever defences the creators of these tools have, one thing is clear: Nintendo won’t like them. And because it doesn’t like them, it will likely try to take them on. However, it might have greater success in pursuing DMCA claims , as it did with Yuzu.

A lot will depend on how the tools used to run Ocarina of Time were made. If they were found to have used tech from Yuzu that was part of Nintendo’s settlement with the creator, they could face trouble. In any case, these tools are running rampant now, and it’s hard to see how legal action can put the genie back in the bottle. If any company were going to tackle this, it would be Nintendo, but that doesn’t mean it’s in for an easy ride.

Rhiannon (she/her) is a freelance journalist who has been in the industry since 2019. She won MCV's Women in Games award in 2025 and adores RPGs. You can follow her on Bluesky at @rhithewitch.
