articles.title: Path of Exile 3.30.0 Covens of Umbra Patch Notes - Path of Exile Guide - IGN
articles.summary: The Covens of Umbra 3.30.0 Patch for Path of Exile has arrived, bringing with it a major Endgame revamp, Item updates, and much
articles.body:
The Covens of Umbra 3.30.0 Patch for Path of Exile has arrived, bringing with it a major Endgame revamp, Item updates, and much more!

This page acts as a comprehensive breakdown of the 3.30 Update for PoE, including a link to the full Patch Notes.

Added a new Intelligence Skill, Arcane Link: Targets an allied player to apply a buff which links you to them for a duration. While linked, they deal additional lightning damage based on your mana. If the target dies while linked, you will also die. This skill cannot be triggered, or used by Totems, Traps, or Mines. It is offered to the Scion for completing Breaking the Seal, and can be purchased from Petarus and Vanja by the Marauder, Duelist and Templar.

Added a new Intelligence Transfigured Skill, Fireball of Radiation: Unleashes a ball of fire ahead that inflicts a short but powerful fire damage over time debuff to each enemy in an area around it.

Added a new Jewel basetype, Mycelium Core.

Added 69 more foiled Tier 17 Valdo's Map options that the Valdo's Puzzle Box can yield.

Added 96 more foiled Unique Item options that the Voidborn Reliquary can yield.

Most Pinnacle content items, Fragments and Keys now have unique audio.

Continued to incrementally improve the sound, art, effects and environments.

The Shaped Region system has been completely reworked.

There are 10 types of Shaped Region, each associated with a specific type of Thread. By default your Atlas has a Shaped Region of each Thread type on it.

Shaped Regions grant affected Maps free Threads of that type. Successfully completing the Shaped Region objective in each Map increases the free Thread count by 1 in all other Maps affected by that Shaped Region.

Completing Shaped Region objectives no longer grants other Maps in that Shaped Region bonus modifiers.

While you have less than 10 Shaped Regions on your Atlas, you can click a button at the centre of the Atlas to Regenerate all Shaped Regions.

Shaped Regions applied by Astrolabes have a higher base number of free Threads applied to Maps in the Region.

Astrolabes have been changed to add a Shaped Region of the specified type to a specific Map on the Atlas, removing existing Shaped Regions of that type from the Atlas.

Astrolabes are no longer restricted from dropping in Shaped Regions.

Templar, Fruiting and Deceptive Astrolabes have been removed. Pre-existing items have been converted to a Cryptic Astrolabe which can be used or vendored to grant a random other Astrolabe.

Scarabs have been removed from the game. A new item type, Threads, have been added in their place.

Threads can be used when entering an Atlas area through the Map Device to apply the associated League mechanic to that Thread to the area. For each Thread expended, up to a maximum of eight, there are also increasingly higher and higher chances to apply powerful randomised transformative effects to the area related to that League mechanic.

Below are the new Thread items available: Abyss Thread Bestiary Thread Betrayal Thread Blight Thread Breach Thread Expedition Thread Incursion Thread Legion Thread Ritual Thread Ultimatum Thread

Added a new Currency Item, Frayed Thread which can be used to grant a random Thread, or vendored for a random Thread.

Existing Scarabs will be converted to either a Thread related to that specific Scarab content, or a Frayed Thread.

Existing Veiled Scarabs will be converted to Frayed Threads.

The majority of Scarab sources throughout the game instead now grants a number of Threads.

A new Threads section has been added to the Fragment Stash Tab, and the Scarabs section is now hidden when empty.

Maven's Chisel of Scarabs has been renamed to Maven's Chisel of Threads, and now increases the quantity of Threads found on a Map (previously Scarabs).

The Skittering Delirium Orb has been renamed to Threaded Delirium Orb, and now grants Thread rewards (previously Scarabs).

Eater of Worlds Altars now have Modifiers that can cause Eldritch Monsters or Map Bosses to drop Breach, Legion, Blight, Ritual or Incursion Threads.

Searing Exarch Altars now have Modifiers that can cause Eldritch Monsters or Map Bosses to drop Abyss, Expedition, Betrayal, Bestiary and Ultimatum Threads.

Eldritch Altar Modifiers that granted a chance for Scarabs dropped by slain Enemies to be Duplicated, instead now apply to Threads.

Strongbox Modifiers that dropped 1-4 of a specific type of Scarab instead now drop 2-5 of a specific type of Thread.

Operative's Strongboxes can no longer be found.

Tormented Heretics now have a base chance to spawn in Maps. Monsters touched by Tormented Heretics have a chance to drop Threads, and monsters possessed by Tormented Heretics drop additional Threads.

The New World Order Achievement now requires completing a Tier 14 or higher Map with at least 8 Threads applied (previously completing a Tier 11 or higher Map with a Horned Scarab applied).

Memory Threads have been renamed to Memory Traces.

The chance for Atlas Anomalies to spawn is now lowered by the amount of monsters remaining in the Map when the Map Boss is killed.

Templar Vaults are no longer granted by Eagon for completing Shaped Regions. Instead, Templar Vaults are now Atlas Anomalies which have a chance to spawn on killing Pinnacle Eldritch Bosses in each specific Atlas quadrant.

Versions of these bosses killed within Maven Invitations or Valdo Maps do not have a chance to spawn these Atlas Anomalies.

The Originator Voidstone no longer causes Equipment Items dropped to have a chance to drop with Memory Strands (note Equipment Items with Memory Strands still drop in Originator-Influenced Maps).

Shaper, Elder and Conqueror Fragments no longer grant increased Item Quantity to Maps, and will no longer be consumed when used along with a Map.

Memory Altar modifiers that enabled Primary League Mechanics such as Abyss, Breach or Legion have been disabled.

Added new Memory Altar modifiers for Ore Deposits, Mercenaries, Beyond, Sentinel, the Viridian Wildwood and Mirage.

Maven's Chisel of Procurement now grants +25% Item Rarity to Maps at 20% Quality (previously 40%).

Item Rarity values on Nightmare and Originator-influenced Map modifiers that specifically augment Item Rarity have been lowered by approximately 40-50%.

Eldritch Altars can now grant 10-20% increased Rarity of Items found in this Area (previously 15-30%).

Memory Trace Altars can now grant 20-25% increased Rarity of Items found in future Areas (previously 25-40%).

The Eldritch and Memory Trace Altars that granted increased Quantity of Items found have been removed.

The Pillars of Arun Unique Map now has 100-150% to Item Rarity (previously 200-300%), and 100-200% increased Experience gain (previously 60-100%).

The following Maps have been added back to the Atlas: Academy, Ancient City, Armoury, Barrows, Bone Crypt, Carcass, Castle Ruins, Coves, Crimson Temple, Cursed Crypt, Defiled Cathedral, Dig, Dungeon, Maze, Moon Temple, Mud Geyser, Necropolis, Overgrown Ruin, Pen, Peninsula, Racecourse, Scriptorium, Sepulchre, Shore, Spider Forest, Thicket, Underground River, Underground Sea, Villa, Waste Pool, and Wasteland.

The following Maps have been removed from the Atlas: Alleyways, Arachnid Tomb, Arsenal, Atoll, Bazaar, Beach, Bramble Valley, Cells, Chateau, Courthouse, Dark Forest, Estuary, Flooded Mine, Forbidden Woods, Forking River, Foundry, Frozen Cabins, Gardens, Ghetto, Infested Valley, Ivory Temple, Lair, Orchard, Pier, Plaza, Primordial Blocks, Shipyard, Stagnation, Toxic Sewer, Vault, and Waterways.

Crafting Recipes are no longer found in Unique Maps. Crafting Recipes for all Meta-Modifiers have been moved to Nightmare Maps instead.

Added four new Meta-Crafting Bench options: 1 Prefix Modifier cannot be changed, for a cost of 1 Divine Orb. 1 Suffix Modifier cannot be changed, for a cost of 1 Divine Orb. 2 Prefix Modifiers cannot be changed, for a cost of 2 Divine Orbs. 2 Suffix Modifiers cannot be changed, for a cost of 2 Divine Orbs.

1 Prefix Modifier cannot be changed, for a cost of 1 Divine Orb.

1 Suffix Modifier cannot be changed, for a cost of 1 Divine Orb.

2 Prefix Modifiers cannot be changed, for a cost of 2 Divine Orbs.

2 Suffix Modifiers cannot be changed, for a cost of 2 Divine Orbs.

The Crafting Bench options for Prefix Modifiers cannot be changed and Suffix Modifiers cannot be changed have had their costs updated, now with differing costs based on item type: Prefixes/Suffixes cannot be changed on Weapons now has a cost of 4 Divine Orbs and 1 Sacred Orb. Prefixes/Suffixes cannot be changed on Armour and Quivers now has a cost of 4 Divine Orbs and 4 Blessed Orbs. Prefixes/Suffixes cannot be changed on Jewellery now has a cost of 4 Divine Orbs and 8 Exalted Orbs.

Prefixes/Suffixes cannot be changed on Weapons now has a cost of 4 Divine Orbs and 1 Sacred Orb.

Prefixes/Suffixes cannot be changed on Armour and Quivers now has a cost of 4 Divine Orbs and 4 Blessed Orbs.

Prefixes/Suffixes cannot be changed on Jewellery now has a cost of 4 Divine Orbs and 8 Exalted Orbs.

The Fractal Gargantuan, Fractal Titan, Synthete Masterpiece and Synthete Nightmare from the Cortex Boss fight now display as Pinnacle Atlas Bosses.

Divine Vessels are now Currency items that can be used on Maps to apply the Deified Enchantment Modifier.

Deified Areas empower all Map Bosses with 25% increased Damage, 25% increased Attack and Cast Speed, 100% increased Toughness, 25% increased Area of Effect, and 50% increased Rarity of items dropped. In Deified areas, you can capture the souls of certain Map Bosses, dropping a filled Divine Vessel on death which can be used to upgrade your Pantheon powers.

Divine Vessels now have a stack size of 20 (previously 1).

Allflame Embers are no longer fragments which can be used alongside a Map. Instead, these are now Currency items which can be used on a Map to apply an Enchantment which provides their pack substitution effect.

Allflame Embers now specify how many Monsters Packs in the area are substituted.

Added three new Allflame Embers: Allflame Ember of the Cloister, Allflame Ember of the Divine, and Allflame Ember of the Multitude.

Mercenary Warrants are no longer fragments you use alongside a Map. Instead they can be used to open portals to the Proving Grounds area on the Atlas, which is an area where you can rematch the previously fought Mercenary.

Delirium Orbs no longer apply enchantments to Maps. Instead they reforge rare Map items with an explicit modifier making players in the area Delirious.

Each Delirium Orb applies between 5 to 50% Delirious percentage.

Applying multiple Delirium Orbs of the same type will add to the current Delirious percentage, up to 100%.

Using a Delirium Orb of a different reward type resets the current Delirious percentage on the Map.

Delirium Orbed Maps have one reward of the specified type and an additional reward of that type for every 20% Delirious Percentage in the area.

Delirium Orbs cannot be used on legacy Maps that have layers of Delirium applied.

The Fragmented Delirium Orb has been removed. Existing Fragmented Delirium Orbs will be converted to Threaded Delirium Orbs.

Existing Maps with Fragmented Delirium Orb Enchantments will instead grant Thread rewards.

The following changes are more prominent at higher area levels: The fog wave from Mirrors of Delirium expands much faster at the start of Delirium encounters. Increased the time before Delirium Fog dissipates. Increased the chance for Delirium Orbs and Cluster Jewels to drop from Delirious monsters. Increased the chance for Delirium Bosses to spawn in Delirium fog. Increased the average stack size of Simulacrum Splinters dropped by Delirium monsters. When starting a Delirium Encounter through a Mirror there is a chance for 1-3 bonus rewards.

The fog wave from Mirrors of Delirium expands much faster at the start of Delirium encounters.

Increased the time before Delirium Fog dissipates.

Increased the chance for Delirium Orbs and Cluster Jewels to drop from Delirious monsters.

Increased the chance for Delirium Bosses to spawn in Delirium fog.

Increased the average stack size of Simulacrum Splinters dropped by Delirium monsters.

When starting a Delirium Encounter through a Mirror there is a chance for 1-3 bonus rewards.

Refracting Fogs now have a small chance to drop from Delirium Bosses in your Tier 14+ Maps. These bosses do not have to be killed within a Mirage to drop a Refracting Fog.

The following league mechanics no longer have a random chance to spawn in Map areas: Abyss, Bestiary, Betrayal, Breach, Blight, Expedition, Incursion, Legion, Ritual, and Ultimatum.

Map areas now have a chance to spawn a Demonic Evocator at the start of the area. Interacting with a Demonic Evocator causes monsters in the area to be able to spawn Beyond portals on death.

Slaying Beyond Bosses in Maps now has a chance to reveal an entrance to a Demonic realm associated with that slain Beyond Boss.

Map Areas now have a small chance to naturally have slaying enemies attract Demons from Beyond.

Beyond Monsters now have an increased chance to drop Tainted Currency.

The chance for Beyond Monsters to spawn portals is now affected by their Monster Power, with Unique Monsters being able to spawn multiple Beyond portals on death.

You now gain Demonic Power for 60 seconds on defeating Beyond Bosses in your Maps.

Beyond Portals no longer stop spawning when slaying enemies after a Beyond Boss has been defeated in an area.

The number of Blight chests in each Lane within Blight encounters in your Maps is now scaled by a percentage of Atlas Drops. Blighted and Blight Ravaged Maps no longer explicitly specify that Atlas Drops scales the number of Blight chests in each Lane.

In Yellow and Red Maps Weeping Essences no longer generate on Monsters, and in Red Maps Wailing Essences no longer generate on Monsters. These changes do not affect Ruthless.

Smuggler's Caches and Sulphite Deposits no longer have a random chance to spawn in Map areas.

Several specific Maps on the Atlas now always spawn Sulphite Veins, or Smuggler's Caches or have a chance to contain a chest with a Forbidden Tome.

Increased the chance for Blueprints from Smuggler's Caches as well as the quantity of Rogue Markers dropped.

Blueprints found in these Maps inherently have a chance to have special Implicit Modifiers.

Fundamentally changed how Items are generated in Path of Exile.

Previously, if a monster drops an item it rolls its "Rarity" (Normal, Magic, Rare or Unique) based on the monster's Item Rarity. If the "Rarity" was not Unique it would then pick from a list of Drop Pools such as Weapons, Rings, Scrolls of Wisdom, Skills Gems, Currency etc to select a specific item to drop.

For example, if the selected "Rarity" was Rare, and the selected Drop Pool was Weapons, then it would generate a random weapon and because the "Rarity" was Rare the weapon would generate as a Rare item. If the selected Drop Pool was Scrolls of Wisdom, then it would generate a Scroll of Wisdom. In this case the monster having more Item Rarity was mostly meaningless as if the selected "Rarity" was Normal, Magic or Rare the item generated would still be a Scroll of Wisdom.

Because of the above, Magic monsters (which have much higher Item Rarity compared to Normal monsters) had 50% less chance to drop items that can't have rarity, such as Currency or Skill Gems, while Rare and Uniques had 80% less chance. This was to prevent the experience of killing a difficult boss and having most of the items that dropped not care about the Item Rarity of that boss.

Item Rarity on monsters and chests has changed to now affect which Drop Pools can be selected. For example, the Scrolls of Wisdom and Portal Scrolls Drop Pools now can only be selected if the generated "Rarity" was normal. This means as monsters have more Item Rarity they will drop fewer Scrolls of Wisdom and Portal Scrolls.

Currency item Drop Pools have been split into a Magic Currency (such as Orbs of Transmutation, Orbs of Alteration, Jeweller's Orbs) and Rare Currency (such as Orbs of Alchemy, Chaos Orbs, Divine Orbs and Mirrors of Kalandra). Magic Currency can only generate if the selected "Rarity" was Magic, and Rare Currency can only generate if the selected "Rarity" was Rare. What this amounts to is the more Item Rarity a monster has, the better the Currency items it drops.

Because high Item Rarity on Monsters now excludes common currencies and increases the chance for valuable currencies, we have removed 50% less chance to drop items that can't have rarity from Magic Monsters, and 80% less from Rare and Unique monsters. As a result, a much greater percentage of valuable currency items you find will now be coming from Rare and Unique Monsters.

Reworked how Modifier Tier Rating works to address two longstanding issues. For context, Modifier Tier Rating is a system used throughout the game to generate Magic and Rare items with higher tier Modifiers.

This first issue was how Modifier Tier Rating can distort the relative chance to see specific types of Modifiers. This is especially noticeable for types of Modifiers with tapering weightings on the higher tier Modifiers, such as increased Physical Damage on weapons. High Modifier Tier Rating would drastically lower the chance to see increased Physical Damage modifiers.

In the new system the chance for a specific type of Modifier to appear is not affected by Modifier Tier Rating.

The second issue was how Modifier Tier Rating lacks granularity, resulting in additional small amounts having little to no impact unless reaching specific value breakpoints where it would have significant impact.

In the new system every bit of Modifier Tier Rating results in higher tier Modifiers on average and there are no longer breakpoints where a large effect is noticed.

articles.title: First Clip From HBO's Harry Potter Series Soundtrack Isn't Going Down Well With Fans
articles.summary: Harry Potter fans have been given a first sample of Hans Zimmer's new HBO series soundtrack, and have complained that it doesn't yet compare to John Williams' beloved movie score.
articles.body:
Harry Potter fans have been given a first sample of Hans Zimmer's new HBO series soundtrack, and have complained that it doesn't yet compare to John Williams' beloved movie score.

Whether you like Harry Potter or not, you will know Hedwig's Theme — the iconic Harry Potter tune penned by legendary composer John Williams which stands alongside the very best of his other creations (Star Wars, Superman, Indiana Jones, and Jaws, to name but a few).

Despite being a hugely accomplished composer himself, Zimmer has a tough act to follow, then — and a first sampling of his new soundtrack for HBO's upcoming Harry Potter series does not seem to be doing him any favors.

🚨🎵PRÉVIA DA MÚSICA PRESENTE NO TRECHO LANÇADO ⚡Harry Potter and the Philosopher's Stone (HBO Original Series Soundtrack) 🎵The Great Feast by Hans Zimmer #HarryPotterHBO — Harry Potter News (@HPTVNews) November 15, 2026

🚨🎵PRÉVIA DA MÚSICA PRESENTE NO TRECHO LANÇADO ⚡Harry Potter and the Philosopher's Stone (HBO Original Series Soundtrack) 🎵The Great Feast by Hans Zimmer #HarryPotterHBO

This track comes from an official clip from the show released by HBO via YouTube which itself met with a decidedly mixed reaction. The scene — which features the start of term banquet — was criticized for its visuals, though there is significant debate online over whether the colorization of the scene has been properly represented. (Earlier peeks at the series were also thought to be washed out compared to the more colourful pallete used in the films.)

Zimmer's sountrack has also come under fire, with unfavourable comments on social media comparing the music to a "Simpsons Hit & Run theme," "those goofy ass copyright free YouTube songs," "if The Sims 1 had a Harry Potter expansion pack," and "Danny Elfman slop." Fans have now extracted the music from the clip and cleared it up for better listening, which you can hear above.

To be fair to Zimmer, this isn't designed to be the series' main theme or anything other than some light-hearted background music while Harry and Ron stuff their faces with roast chicken and cake. But as the first bit of music from the series to be released, fans are inevitably drawing conclusions about the rest of the soundtrack.

Harry Potter and the Philosopher's Stone TV Show Character Images

Zimmer's involvement in the series was announced earlier this year, when it was confirmed that the composer of Interstellar, The Dark Knight Trilogy, Gladiator and countless other blockbusters would be working with Kara Talve and Anže Rozman from Bleeding Fingers Music, an Emmy Award-winning collective of muscians he co-founded, to produce the new series' score.

"The musical legacy of Harry Potter is a touch point for composers everywhere and we are humbled to join such a remarkable team on a project of this magnitude," Zimmer said at the time. "The responsibility is something that myself, Kara Talve and Anže Rozman do not take lightly. Magic is all around us, often just beyond reach, but as in the world of Harry Potter, you simply must look for it. With this score we hope to bring audiences that little bit closer to it whilst honoring what has come before."

Just over a month remains until HBO debuts the first episode of its Harry Potter series on December 25, with episodes then following regularly into early 2027. Last month brought a fresh wave of casting confirmations , including Shameless and Fargo actor William H. Macy as the Sorting Hat.

articles.title: After Microsoft offers buyouts to 60,000 employees, CEO Satya Nadella explains the decision; says: I wish I could just sit here and ...
articles.summary: Microsoft CEO Satya Nadella has addressed the question over the tech giant’s massive new buyout program and whether this is a sign of upcoming AI-driven
articles.body: Microsoft CEO Satya Nadella has addressed the question over the tech giant’s massive new buyout program and whether this is a sign of upcoming AI-driven layoffs, explaining that the company is reshaping how its teams work rather than simply shrinking its headcount. Speaking after Microsoft rolled out a Voluntary Exit Offer (VEO) to roughly 60,000 workers, which is more than a quarter of its global staff—Nadella emphasized that the future of the company will look noticeably different in terms of team sizes and daily workflows.“It’s a very important question. Let’s acknowledge that there is going to be plenty of opportunity going forward. The shape of that opportunity may be different,” Nadella said, adding, “The shape of what this new thing looks like is going to be different than what it was before: team sizes and team workflows.” While Nadella stressed that he wants all 200,000-plus Microsoft employees to grow and flourish, he noted that the workforce “will have to be configured in different ways.”Microsoft CEO Satya Nadella: ‘Vote with your feet’According to the CEO, the voluntary buyout is designed to give employees control over their careers as the company evolves, especially for those sitting in units that have been slow to adapt.“This voluntary thing was mostly about letting everybody have more agency to get themselves into places that make sense for their economic opportunity long term. That's, I think, the key thing. I don't want to be stuck in a team that's not transforming, even inside of Microsoft. Let's face it. It's not like I can sit here and say every part of Microsoft has really got the memo," Nadella explained at The Pragmatic Engineer podcast.He added that employees who feel professionally stuck now have the option to leave on good terms, though he encouraged them to explore internal transfers first.“If you're in a team where you feel stuck professionally, you can vote with your feet. I don't want you to, because quite frankly there are many places you can go inside of Microsoft itself. I wish I could just sit here and say it'll all be the same. I cannot. And this is one of those places where I want to be as transparent about the change,” Nadella said.What was Microsoft’s buyout offerChief people officer Amy Coleman announced the Voluntary Exit Offer in a memo to staff, framing it as a chance for employees already considering a move outside Microsoft to exit now with financial backing and career support. The offer applies to eligible staff at internal level 70 and below, which is a group that includes roles up to general managers and some vice presidents, across just four countries: The US, Canada, The UK and India.Unlike Microsoft’s spring retirement buyout, this offer has no age or tenure minimums and job performance is not a factor. Eligible workers have until the first week of December to decide, with departures set for the end of the year.The buyout terms match Microsoft’s standard severance package. During US layoffs earlier this year, severance included at least 60 days of base pay on the payroll and up to 39 weeks of base pay depending on seniority and tenure – giving employees at level 64 and below one week of base pay per six months of service, and those at levels 65 to 67 two weeks per six months.The VEO also covers continued stock vesting, career transition help, and healthcare coverage for a fixed period. Unlike the earlier retirement program, however, it does not include extended healthcare benefits. Individual terms are being sent via email to eligible staff, including those in India.This marks Microsoft’s second major buyout push in 2026 following waves of layoffs over the past two years. In 2025 cuts, Microsoft eliminated more than 15,000 jobs.This year, the company launched its first-ever Voluntary Retirement Program for about 8,750 US staff (senior director level and below) whose age and years of service totaled at least 70. Microsoft laid off 4,800 workers (around 2% of its workforce) in July, hitting Xbox and commercial sales hardest, followed by hundreds more cuts in September.Your child uses AI every day. articles.title: The Impossible Mission of Getting GTA 5's Seamless Character Switching Working on PS3 and Xbox 360
articles.summary: How a former Rockstar developer made GTA 5's seamless character switching work on PS3 and Xbox 360.
articles.body:
One of the key innovations in GTA 5 is about to be replicated in GTA 6 — character switching. We've already seen this in the trailers, as the player switched control between driver and gunner while evading police. While GTA 6 features dual protagonists, Jason and Lucia, you can freely switch between, GTA 5 had three of them: Franklin, Trevor, and Michael. Out in the open world, you could switch and the camera would shoot into the sky for a satellite view of the city before zooming back down to the character you’d chosen.

That satellite view was a fancy way of hiding a loading screen while getting across the scale of Los Santos at the same time. In-mission character switches were a different, more complicated problem though.

“During the heist missions — I don't think a lot of people noticed this because we were doing it so seamlessly — we would have swaps between characters that were on completely different sides of the map, and we were not allowed to go to that satellite screen to mask the loading,” Matt Freedman, who was a technical designer on the game working out of Rockstar Toronto, told IGN.

Freedman worked at Rockstar for almost nine years, starting as a level designer for Max Payne 3 before moving onto a technical design role for GTA 5 and a wider game design role on Red Dead Redemption 2. For GTA 5 he designed and implemented this complex player character switching system that allowed cinematic and dynamic open-world switching sequences mid-mission.

“So, effectively, like we were trying to get like an NVMe-speed world transition, like the kind of stuff that they would have in like the portal sequence for Ratchet & Clank [on a PS5 SSD], and trying to get that to run on a PS3 and an Xbox 360. I probably spent two years on what amounts to about two, maybe three minutes of actual gameplay.”

Initially, Freedman achieved this through clever camera tricks, such as starting the switched character leaning against a wall with the camera zoomed in on their hand, giving the world around them a chance to load before the player took control. For the perfectionists at Rockstar leadership, this wasn’t good enough because players didn’t get to see the star of the show: the city itself.

“I’d always get these notes saying, ‘No, no, we have to see the city skyline,’” Freedman explained. “I'm like, ‘Let me tell you how loading works on our engine. We cannot have two copies of the city loaded at the same time. We need to allow this stuff to go into memory.’ At the end of the project, those weren't recommendations; those were mandates. You had to see the city skyline.

“Details matter. I was very proud of the system that we made, and the fact that it held up so well. And like, you do see a little bit of streaming when we do the transition, but it's usually very far in the distance.”

Freedman made it work by implementing gradual level-of-detail (LOD) changes based on radius from the player. Distant traffic became single light sources, far buildings became flat and undefined, the lack of detail masked by smart use of depth of field effects. The designers would ensure the character was always doing something interesting so the skyline became a backdrop rather than a focal point.

“We then would very rapidly turn on those streaming systems,” Freedman said. “And like you know, if you wanted to sit there with a sniper rifle and look off in the distance, you would see things loading in. But most players didn't do that.

It wasn’t just streaming textures that caused problems with character switching, either. A good example is the mission Three’s Company, where the trio of criminals have to extract a terrorist suspect from the IAA building — a huge skyscraper in the middle of Los Santos’ downtown area with the sprawl of the city all around it.

Trevor flies a helicopter in, Franklin sits across from the building on another rooftop with a sniper rifle, and Michael rappels down the building from the helicopter to stage the hostage retrieval. Players switch between all three characters, the city stretched out below and seen from multiple angles, and the camera has to zip between the characters in a few seconds — one of which is hanging from a rope, another flying a helicopter the player can freely control.

“We had to put in so much tech to make sure that we were respecting any player's gameplay choices because that helicopter kept screwing us because it can be upside down, it can be banking, it can be doing anything,” Freedman explained. “Whenever I work on something, taking away player control is never the answer. If we literally are hours away from shipping the game, I will consider it. But until then, I will put in the hours to keep that player control there.

“The camera normally would just do a straight interpolation between two points (rotation and position). However, because the helicopter can potentially have an arbitrary rotation and position, it would oftentimes wind up with a transition to or from it that felt to the player that it was moving in the wrong direction — for example if the helicopter was upside down, then the player would see the camera seeming to flip, then go downwards instead of up.”

Character switching ended up being one of GTA 5’s defining features, but Freedman initially thought players wouldn’t notice. When reviews dropped, however, one at a major outlet featured a montage of his team’s work, highlighting the slick camera transitions.

“It was me and another designer who were working on these at the same time,” Freedman remembered. “We were having a competition with each other over who did the best ones, and he came over to my desk. He's like, ‘Check out the GameSpot review, five of yours and five of mine.’ And that was he was right. They showed exactly five of my transitions and five of his transitions. So we're like, ‘All right, at the end, we tied.’ But I think that was one of my proudest moments.”

On the eve of GTA 6's release, it's systems like seamless character swapping in the previous game that have cemented Rockstar's reputation for insane level of detail and high quality. And we're just hours away from seeing it in action in GTA 6 for ourselves.

While you wait for GTA 6 to unlock we've got loads of great coverage for you to check out, including Gangland Tales From the Frontline of Rockstar's Real-Life Grand Theft Auto Research , and How Gaming's Top Content Creators Are Preparing for GTA 6's Launch and Beyond .

articles.title: Nintendo Suffers Rare Review Bombing For Pikmin 4: Nintendo Switch 2 Edition + Dandori Academy
articles.summary: Nintendo fans are hitting the company with a rare review bombing campaign, to register their dissatisfaction with Pikmin 4: Nintendo Switch 2 Edition + Dandori Academy.
articles.body:
Nintendo fans are hitting the company with a rare review bombing campaign, to register their dissatisfaction with Pikmin 4: Nintendo Switch 2 Edition + Dandori Academy .

The Switch 2 upgrade for Nintendo's brilliant Pikmin 4 launched last week as a paid add-on, priced $9.99. It adds a fresh challenge mode, Dandori Academy, and bumps up the overall package's visuals to 4K.

All of that sounds like fun, and it is (I submitted my times for all of the first batch of courses this weekend!) but fans are pushing back on what they argue is reused and repackaged content, as well as a knock to the game's loading times.

Each month, six new challenge levels will be available to practice, with the ability to file competitive times during a limited time window each weekend. But these aren't all-new challenge levels, and instead are a mixture of fresh maps mixed with repeats from the base game's original Dandori mode, as well as modified versions of existing campaign areas.

It's been a while since I played Pikmin 4's campaign, so this didn't initially register to me — but YouTuber Press A! has presented a look at how some "new" Dandori levels are just dungeon caves from the base game with slight tweaks, and multiple versions of these same levels already — with some just rotated to be viewed from a different orientation. Who knows what the future holds for future batches of levels, but with just this crop available to fans right now, players are drawing their own conclusions.

And then there's the loading times. Initial evidence shows a hit of up to 30 seconds in-game when emerging from a cave in the game's story mode, in comparison to the Switch 1 version. Here's hoping Nintendo sees the feedback here and can tweak some settings behind the scenes, as this clearly feels like an area for improvement.

"DO NOT Buy THIS!" wrote one user on Metacritic , where Pikmin 4: Nintendo Switch 2 Edition + Dandori Academy has hundreds of negative reviews and a "generally unfavourable" user score. "This is a big let down and nowhere near as good as old Pikmin 4 is. My game had terrible loading times after getting this and they took forever. The new mode is boring and has copied levels. Graphics are good but they are the only good thing. I regret buying the Switch 2 Edition."

"It feels like more of a downgrade then an upgrade of the game," wrote another. "Longer loads and freezing up in game and the Dandori mode is most of the same stuff from what was in the game already."

It's a shame to see this response towards Pikmin 4, as the base game is a joyful experience and arguably the best game yet in Nintendo's garden strategy series. While this upgrade was likely always going to be a stopgap before the (hopefully!) inevitable Pikmin 5, it does feel like there was more room for improvement in a franchise that's still looking to appear to more fans — rather than disappoint those who were on board already.

articles.title: Elsinore Is a Hollow Quest for an Award for Star Andrew Scott
articles.summary: Elsinore review: A hollow quest for an award for star Andrew Scott.
articles.body:
Another award season, another Shakespeare-adjacent film starring a well-liked actor who is apparently overdue for their state mandated awards campaign. Yes, since Jessie Buckley soared straight to an Oscar win last year for playing the Bard’s long-suffering wife Agnes in Chloé Zhao’s pretty good historical drama Hamnet, apparently it’s now time for another thespian to make a claim for the throne. This time it’s the ever-reliable Andrew Scott — an actor I’m never mad to see pop up in anything — working with director Simon Stone, who I’ve never had a strong opinion about one way or the other. The Swiss-born Australian filmmaker claims a profound love for Shakespeare’s works, so it makes sense for him to jump at the chance to direct a movie about a man who would do anything to make his mark playing Hamlet before he dies. If only such passion had also managed to conjure up a good reason for the film to exist.

Elsinore, named for the castle where the events of the play Hamlet take place, stars Scott as Scottish actor Ian Charleson, an actor most famous for his work in 1981's Chariots of Fire and for later succumbing to AIDS after his National Theatre run as Hamlet in late 1989. The film dramatizes Charleson’s battle with the disease while under the care of Margaret Johnson (Olivia Colman), one of the UK’s earliest specialists in treating HIV/AIDS. Charleson’s drive to play the Prince of Denmark knowing he will most likely die in the process is as relatable and unerringly human as many of the dramatic impulses present in the play’s cast of characters. But the film’s construction — the pieces that are supposed to make it compelling as a visual story — short-change that emotional core more often than it can endure.

For a movie about a man dying of AIDS, Elsinore is far too blandly amiable. Charleson’s malaise with the results of his acting career and polite contempt for the smattering of fame he’s received are a good place to start, but he’s surrounded by too many good-natured and dramatically vacant supporting characters who basically exist to tell him he’s strong for toughing it out. Billie Piper is on hand as Patsy, Charleson’s token straight friend who offers him soup and smiles, and Johnny Flynn plays Richard Eyre, Charleson’s director who is only too understanding that his leading man may just collapse and die mid-performance. Even Colman’s Johnson, who routinely scolds Charleson for putting Hamlet ahead of his health, is tuned to more of an annoyance than an antagonist. Colman can trade barbs with the best of them, but there’s never any doubt that her Very Concerned resolve will ultimately melt in the face of Charleson’s peppy determination to make his eight o’clock curtain.

The only person who actually challenges Charleson is Derek Jarman (David Dawson), the man who directed Charleson in the 1978 film, Jubilee. A fellow artist living with HIV, Jarman thinks Charleson is a sell-out for not living openly as a gay man and continuing to work with queer artists, and that Charleson’s desire for mainstream appeal is a disservice to the generation of gay men who are dropping like flies from the disease they share. Charleson’s rebuke that he doesn’t owe his life choices to anyone but himself, that he considers himself an actor more than an AIDS patient, is not only one of the film’s best scenes but also one of the only moments where Stephen Beresford’s screenplay depicts its subject as anything more than a summary. Elsinore may have a lot of drama on the stage, but it’s severely lacking in such on the page.

For his part, Scott is very good here. His precise but unfussy inhabitation of Charleson’s doomed conviviality is the number one reason to see Elsinore, and it will almost assuredly get him into the awards conversation as everyone involved intended. The way Scott manages to convey softly spoken but biting remarks as a critical point of character rather than an obtrusive affectation is commendable, as is his tenderness with the other patients that never belies false hope in their odds of survival. The scenes of Charleson rehearsing his lines and finding how he will channel his frustrations and anxieties into his performance as Hamlet are among the moments where the film really does come alive.

Sadly, Stone’s direction doesn’t do much to back Scott up. The flat colors and coherent but uninspired cinematography is all in service of not getting in the way of his actors’ legibility. It's a noble goal, but it makes the film anonymous on a formal level. Nor does it matter when the edit undermines Scott’s work; Stone chops up important scenes, including Charleson on the stage, as montages instead of letting them actually play out. I don’t understand why you would hire a lead actor with years of theater experience — including a run playing Hamlet — and not just let him play Hamlet. That we don’t get five to ten uninterrupted minutes of just seeing Scott as Charleson giving his final performance — the one the movie has spent its whole runtime insisting is so important — is such a bizarre choice that I simply sat there confused as the credits rolled.
